description:
Something went quiet on Mars.

Years later, we still can’t stop hearing it.

We’re Team Dormant, two friends who keep calling out to a machine that was only meant to last a season. We’re building a story you don’t read; you uncover. Dark screen. Static. Press play, and Mars answers.

As someone who sees in color, hears in sound, and builds worlds in code. Come find out what’s on the other end.

Hello, Mars?
summary: For the NASA Space Challenge Hackathon 2026, we crafted an immersive storytelling journey chronicling the Kepler Space Telescope—a marvel engineered to spot distant worlds by catching a firefly’s whisper of starlight. Overcoming initial rejections and devastating reaction-wheel failures, Kepler was ingeniously reborn as the K2 mission, harnessing solar radiation pressure to unlock thousands of exoplanets, including habitable-zone pioneers Kepler-22b and Kepler-186f. By transforming complex astrophysics into a gripping human narrative, our project illustrates how sheer ingenuity reshaped our cosmic perspective and paved the way for modern successors like TESS and the James Webb Space Telescope
details:
For the NASA Space Challenge Hackathon 2026, we developed an immersive, narrative-driven storytelling website dedicated to the Kepler Space Telescope.

What the project does and how it works : It chronicles humanity’s transition from knowing of only a single planetary system to discovering thousands of alien worlds by utilizing the transit method—detecting microscopic, regular dips in starlight as small as 84 parts per million when a planet crosses its host star.

What benefits it has & its intended impact : The project makes complex aerospace engineering and astrophysics deeply accessible and engaging, reframing how people understand our place in the cosmos, highlighting engineering resilience through the K2 revival, and honoring how Kepler's vast data archive paves the way for modern successors like TESS and the James Webb Space Telescope.

Tools used : We integrated the core mission chapters, telemetry data, and technical milestones from Kepler's archives into a structured, multi-stage narrative flow. Creativity & team considerations : Our team focused heavily on human-centric storytelling—transforming a mechanical failure into a triumphant narrative arc by highlighting William Borucki's persistence, the transition from initial rejection to launch in 2009, and the brilliant K2 mission rescue strategy using solar radiation pressure.
